cues.zh: 这位画家，把芭蕾舞演员的头切掉了。你看舞台上，只剩下裙子和腿。
cues.en: This painter cut off the dancers' heads. Look at the stage: only skirts and legs are left.

cues.zh: 观众买票，本来是去看演员的。可德加偏偏把平时没人注意的乐手放在最前面，一张张脸都画得很清楚。
cues.en: People bought tickets to see the dancers. But Degas put the musicians nobody notices right up front, and painted every face clearly.

cues.zh: 大家花钱来看的，他为什么偏偏切掉？
cues.en: Why cut off the very thing people paid to see?

cues.zh: 一百五十年前，德加和他朋友们的画挂出来，很多人看了直笑，说它们根本没画完。这群人被称为印象派画家。
cues.en: A hundred and fifty years ago, when paintings by Degas and his friends were hung, people laughed at them. They said the paintings weren't even finished. These painters came to be called the Impressionists.

cues.zh: 「印象派」这个名字是从哪里来的？从一篇嘲笑它们的文章里来的。
cues.en: And where did the name "Impressionist" come from? From an article that made fun of them.

cues.zh: 可今天，同样这些画，人们排着队去看。画上一笔都没变，变的是什么？
cues.en: Yet today, people line up to see the very same paintings. Not one brushstroke has changed. So what changed?

cues.zh: 印象派的魅力在哪里？
cues.en: What is the charm of Impressionism?

cues.zh: 你知道印象派的秘密吗？
cues.en: Do you know the secret of Impressionism?

cues.zh: 今天每一位画家，我们都问一个问题：在他眼里，什么最重要，什么可以去掉？
cues.en: So for every painter today, we'll ask one question: in their eyes, what mattered most, and what could be left out?

cues.zh: 故事要从十九世纪的巴黎说起。那时候画家想出名，几乎只有一条路：把画送进官方的大展览，叫「沙龙」。
cues.en: Our story begins in nineteenth-century Paris. If a painter wanted to be famous, there was almost only one road: get your work into the big official exhibition, the Salon.

cues.zh: 比如沙龙展览上，梅索尼埃画的拿破仑行军，你看见了什么？
cues.en: Take this painting from the Salon: Meissonier's Napoleon on the march. What do you see?

cues.zh: 每一匹马的缰绳、雪地上每一道车辙，都画得清清楚楚。
cues.en: Every horse's reins, every rut in the snow, painted crystal clear.

cues.zh: 一般认为，沙龙喜欢的画，画面要光滑，笔触要藏起来，细节越完整越好。
cues.en: It's generally said that the Salon liked smooth surfaces, hidden brushstrokes, and as much detail as possible.

cues.zh: 1839 年，照相术问世了。论细节，画家再怎么画，也比不过相机。
cues.en: In 1839, photography arrived. For detail, no painter could ever beat a camera.

cues.zh: 后来，照相机还拍下了马奔跑时每一刻的样子。连梅索尼埃也承认，这些照片改变了他对马怎么跑的看法。画得再细，也可能是错的。
cues.en: Later, cameras even caught a running horse, moment by moment. Meissonier himself admitted the photographs changed his idea of how a horse moves. More detail can still be wrong.

cues.zh: 那画家还要画什么？
cues.en: So what was left for painters to paint?

cues.zh: 下面这几位画家，各自给了自己的回答。
cues.en: Each of the painters we're about to meet gave an answer of their own.

cues.zh: 接下来要看的《草地上的午餐》和《奥林匹亚》，画里都有裸体。它们都是艺术史上的重要作品。不想看的话，可以现在按进度条，跳到下一章「马奈莫奈」。
cues.en: The next two paintings, Luncheon on the Grass and Olympia, both include nudity. Both are important works in art history. If you would rather skip them, use the progress bar now to jump to the next chapter, “Manet and Monet.”

cues.zh: 第一位是爱德华·马奈。他比莫奈大八岁多，年轻画家都把他当榜样，可他自己从来没参加过印象派的展览。他对朋友说过：沙龙，才是真正的战场。
cues.en: First, Édouard Manet. He was eight years older than Monet, and younger painters looked up to him. Yet he never once showed at the Impressionist exhibitions. "The Salon," he told a friend, "is the real field of battle."

cues.zh: 1863 年，沙龙落选的画太多，皇帝拿破仑三世下令另开一个「落选者沙龙」。马奈的《草地上的午餐》在那里引起了轩然大波。
cues.en: In 1863, the Salon turned away so many paintings that Emperor Napoleon the Third ordered a second show: the Salon of the Refused. There, Manet's Luncheon on the Grass caused an uproar.

cues.zh: 两年后，他又送去一幅画。就是下面要看的这幅《奥林匹亚》。
cues.en: Two years later, he sent in another painting. It was Olympia, the painting we are about to see.

cues.zh: 《奥林匹亚》画于 1863 年，1865 年在沙龙展出。
cues.en: Manet painted Olympia in 1863, and showed it at the Salon of 1865.

cues.zh: 它的构图，几乎照搬了三百多年前提香的名画《乌尔比诺的维纳斯》：同样躺着，同样的姿势。
cues.en: Its layout is borrowed, almost exactly, from a famous painting three hundred years older: Titian's Venus of Urbino. The same reclining figure, the same pose.

cues.zh: 可是有几处不一样。你找得到吗？
cues.en: But a few things are different. Can you find them?

cues.zh: 提香的维纳斯也看着你，眼神很柔和，脚边睡着一只小狗；马奈的奥林匹亚看你的眼神，冷静又直接，脚边是一只弓着背的黑猫。
cues.en: Titian's Venus looks at you too, softly, with a little dog asleep at her feet. Manet's Olympia looks at you calmly and directly, and at her feet stands a black cat with its back arched.

cues.zh: 最大的不同是：提香画的是女神，马奈画的是当时巴黎的一个妓女。
cues.en: The biggest change: Titian painted a goddess. Manet painted a prostitute in the Paris of his own time.

cues.zh: 那个年代的沙龙可以接受吗？裸体只能是女神、是神话。
cues.en: Would the Salon of that time accept her? Nudes there had to be goddesses, figures from myth.

cues.zh: 马奈没有给她女神的身份。光从正面直直地打在她身上，几乎没有柔和的阴影，身体看起来是平的。
cues.en: Manet didn't make her a goddess. The light falls straight on her from the front, with hardly any soft shadow, and her body looks flat.

cues.zh: 她就这样直直地看着我们。马奈为什么要这样画？
cues.en: And she looks straight back at us. Why did Manet paint her this way?

cues.zh: 当年的人们没有问为什么。展览上，观众围着它嘲笑、叫骂。
cues.en: Back then, people didn't ask why. At the exhibition, crowds gathered round it to laugh and jeer.

cues.zh: 1865 年的那届沙龙上，还挂着两幅海景，作者叫莫奈。马奈看见这个跟自己这么像的名字，以为有人在模仿他。
cues.en: At that same Salon of 1865 hung two seascapes by a painter named Monet. Manet saw a name so like his own, and thought someone was copying him.

cues.zh: 据他的朋友迪雷回忆，马奈很不高兴：这个莫奈是谁？好像拿了我的名字，来沾我闹出的动静！
cues.en: His friend Théodore Duret remembered Manet grumbling: "Who is this Monet? He seems to have taken my name, to profit from all the stir I'm making!"

cues.zh: 马奈和莫奈，法文名字只差一个字母。第二年，漫画家吉尔干脆在漫画下面写：是莫奈，还是马奈？
cues.en: Manet and Monet: one letter apart. The next year, the cartoonist Gill simply wrote under his drawing: "Monet or Manet?"

cues.zh: 迪雷还说，从那以后，莫奈签名总在姓前面写上「克劳德」。
cues.en: Duret also says that from then on, Monet always signed with "Claude" in front of his surname.

cues.zh: 1866 年，马奈画了这个吹笛少年，走得更远。你看他身后，有什么？
cues.en: In 1866, Manet painted this young fifer, and went even further. Look behind him. What's there?

cues.zh: 背景里没有墙，没有地板，没有房间，只有一片灰。
cues.en: No wall, no floor, no room. Just gray.

cues.zh: 少年身上也几乎没有慢慢过渡的阴影：红裤子就是一块红，黑上衣就是一块黑。
cues.en: And hardly any gentle shading on the boy himself. The red trousers are simply red. The black jacket is simply black.

cues.zh: 马奈去掉了房间，也去掉了慢慢过渡的阴影。
cues.en: Manet left out the room, and he left out the gentle shading.

cues.zh: 这幅画被 1866 年的沙龙拒绝了。可作家左拉在报上写：我不相信，还能用更简单的手段，得到更强有力的效果。
cues.en: The Salon of 1866 rejected it. But the writer Émile Zola wrote in a newspaper: "I do not think it is possible to obtain a more powerful effect with less complicated means."

cues.zh: 马奈上中学时，读到狄德罗的一句话：一个民族的衣着要是寒碜，艺术就该把服装撇开。这其实是在讲追求理想化的纯粹美。
cues.en: When Manet was at school, he read a line by Diderot: "When a people's dress is mean, art should leave the costume aside." In other words, art should reach for an ideal, pure beauty.

cues.zh: 他对同学说：这太蠢了。人要属于自己的时代，画自己看到的东西。
cues.en: Manet told his classmate: "How foolish. One must be of one's own time, and paint what one sees."

cues.zh: 你看这幅《铁路》。题目叫铁路，可火车在哪儿？
cues.en: Look at The Railway. It's called The Railway, but where's the train?

cues.zh: 只有栏杆后面一大团白色的蒸汽。
cues.en: Just a big cloud of white steam behind the railings.

cues.zh: 小女孩望着蒸汽，旁边的女士抬头看了我们一眼。马奈为什么不画火车？
cues.en: The girl watches the steam. The woman beside her glances up at us. Why didn't Manet paint the train?

cues.zh: 后来，马奈和莫奈成了好朋友。1874 年夏天，马奈住到塞纳河对岸，画下了在小船上画画的莫奈。
cues.en: In time, Manet and Monet became good friends. In the summer of 1874, Manet stayed across the river from Monet, and painted him at work in his little studio boat.

cues.zh: 1874 年春天，莫奈、雷诺阿、德加、毕沙罗、莫里索、塞尚，一共三十位艺术家，不再等沙龙，自己办了一场展览。
cues.en: In the spring of 1874, Monet, Renoir, Degas, Pissarro, Morisot, Cézanne, thirty artists in all, stopped waiting for the Salon and put on their own exhibition.

cues.zh: 莫奈送去的一幅画，就是《印象·日出》。你的评价是什么？
cues.en: One of the paintings Monet sent was Impression, Sunrise. What do you think of it?

cues.zh: 评论家勒鲁瓦写了一篇讽刺文章，让一位虚构的老派画家看着它大叫：刚起稿的糊墙纸，都比这幅海景画得完整！
cues.en: The critic Louis Leroy wrote a mocking review, and had an imaginary old-school painter cry out: "Wallpaper in its embryonic state is more finished than that seascape!"

cues.zh: 「印象派」这个名字，就是从这篇嘲笑的文章里来的。他们后来一共办了八次展览，从 1874 年一直到 1886 年。
cues.en: The name "Impressionists" came from that mocking article. They went on to hold eight exhibitions, from 1874 to 1886.

cues.zh: 当年的观众为什么看不懂？这些画家又为什么偏不照沙龙的规矩画？
cues.en: Why couldn't people back then understand these paintings? And why did these painters refuse to follow the Salon's rules?

cues.zh: 我们一位一位来看。
cues.en: Let's look at them one by one.

cues.zh: 在莫奈眼里，什么可以去掉？美国女画家佩里，记下了他说过的一段话：
cues.en: In Monet's eyes, what could be left out? The American painter Lilla Cabot Perry wrote down something he told her:

cues.zh: 出去画画的时候，试着忘掉你面前是什么东西，一棵树、一座房子、一片田。只想：这里是一小块蓝，这里是一长条粉，这里是一道黄。
cues.en: "When you go out to paint, try to forget what objects you have before you, a tree, a house, a field. Merely think: here is a little square of blue, here an oblong of pink, here a streak of yellow."

cues.zh: 照它看起来的样子画，颜色和形状都要准确，直到画出你自己对眼前景色最天真的印象。
cues.en: "And paint it just as it looks to you, the exact color and shape, until it gives your own naive impression of the scene before you."

cues.zh: 据她回忆，莫奈还说过：真希望自己生下来是瞎的，后来忽然看得见了，这样就能不知道眼前是什么东西，直接这样去画。
cues.en: She remembered that he wished he had been born blind and then suddenly gained his sight, so he could paint without knowing what the objects before him were.

cues.zh: 来看这幅《撑阳伞的女人》。画的是他的妻子卡米耶和儿子让。
cues.en: Look at Woman with a Parasol. It's his wife, Camille, and their son, Jean.

cues.zh: 仔细看她的脸。你看得清吗？
cues.en: Look closely at her face. Can you see it clearly?

cues.zh: 几乎没有画。眼睛、鼻子、嘴，都看不清。
cues.en: It's barely painted. Eyes, nose, mouth: you can't make them out.

cues.zh: 画面里看得最清楚的，反倒是风：被吹起的裙摆，飘动的面纱，草被风压弯的方向，还有逆着光的天空。
cues.en: What you can see most clearly is the wind: the billowing skirt, the floating veil, the grass bent one way, and the bright sky behind her.

cues.zh: 画自己的妻子，脸只有几笔，风却画得清清楚楚。为什么？
cues.en: His own wife's face, in just a few strokes, and the wind painted in full. Why?

cues.zh: 1890 年，他在给朋友若弗鲁瓦的信里写：我要找的，是「瞬间」，尤其是包住一切的那层光；一挥而就的容易东西，我越来越讨厌。
cues.en: In 1890 he wrote to his friend Gustave Geffroy that what he was seeking was "instantaneity," above all the envelope of light over everything, and that easy things, done at the first try, disgusted him more and more.

cues.zh: 其实早在 1877 年，莫奈就走进巴黎的圣拉扎尔火车站，画站里的蒸汽和光，一共画了十二幅。
cues.en: As early as 1877, Monet had walked into the Saint-Lazare station in Paris to paint its steam and light, twelve times over.

cues.zh: 他一辈子在户外、在各种天气里画，一直画到八十多岁。
cues.en: All his life he painted outdoors, in every kind of weather, into his eighties.

cues.zh: 可是在这些光里，有一个人一次又一次出现。她就是撑阳伞的卡米耶，莫奈的第一任妻子。
cues.en: But in all that light, one person appears again and again: the woman with the parasol, Camille, Monet's first wife.

cues.zh: 1866 年，莫奈画了穿绿裙子的卡米耶，送进沙龙，得到不少称赞。
cues.en: In 1866 Monet painted Camille in a green dress, and it won plenty of praise at the Salon.

cues.zh: 花园里、长椅上、窗外的雪地里，到处都是她。在好几幅画里，她的脸只有几笔。
cues.en: In the garden, on a bench, in the snow outside the window, she's everywhere. In several of these paintings, her face is just a few strokes.

cues.zh: 1879 年，卡米耶病逝，只有三十二岁。莫奈在她床前，画下了最后一幅。
cues.en: In 1879, Camille died. She was only thirty-two. Monet painted her one last time, at her bedside.

cues.zh: 很多年以后，他对朋友克列孟梭说：在一位至今深爱的女人灵前，他竟然发现自己的眼睛在找她脸上颜色的变化，蓝、黄、灰。
cues.en: Many years later, he told his friend Georges Clemenceau that beside a woman who was still very dear to him, he caught his own eyes searching her face for the changing colors: blues, yellows, grays.

cues.zh: 德加一直不肯接受「印象派」这个叫法，他宁愿说自己是写实派、独立派。他最爱画的是剧院、芭蕾和巴黎街头。
cues.en: Degas never accepted the name "Impressionist." He preferred to call himself a Realist, or an Independent. What he loved to paint were theaters, ballet, and the streets of Paris.

cues.zh: 还记得开头那幅画吗？那些没有头的芭蕾舞演员？那就是德加的《歌剧院的乐队》，大约 1870 年画的。
cues.en: Remember the painting we started with, the dancers with no heads? That's Degas's The Orchestra at the Opera, from about 1870.

cues.zh: 乐池里这些人，都是真实的人，有名有姓。正中间吹巴松管的迪奥，是德加的朋友；这幅画后来就收藏在他家里。
cues.en: The people in the orchestra pit are real people, each with a name. In the middle, playing the bassoon, is Désiré Dihau, a friend of Degas. The painting later belonged to him.

cues.zh: 他为什么要切掉她们？
cues.en: So why did he cut the dancers off?

cues.zh: 我们再看他的两幅画。
cues.en: Let's look at two more of his paintings.

cues.zh: 再看这幅《协和广场》。你看到了什么？
cues.en: Here's Place de la Concorde. What do you see?

cues.zh: 一位先生带着两个女儿和一条狗，可他们都往画面边上走，正中间空荡荡的。
cues.en: A gentleman, his two daughters and a dog, all walking off toward the edges, and the middle is empty.

cues.zh: 《舞蹈课》也一样。你看到了什么？
cues.en: The Dance Class is like that too. What do you see?

cues.zh: 只有一个女孩在跳，其他人在等，在发呆，在整理头发和裙子。
cues.en: Only one girl is dancing. The others wait, daydream, fix their hair and skirts.

cues.zh: 可他为什么偏要切掉舞者、留下乐手，画排练的空档、不画演出？
cues.en: So why cut off the dancers and keep the musicians? Why paint the waiting in between, and not the show?

cues.zh: 我们不知道。但是我们可以更了解德加。
cues.en: We don't know. But we can get to know Degas better.

cues.zh: 据作家乔治·摩尔记录，德加常说：没有哪一种艺术，比我的更不即兴；我画的，是思考和研究古代大师的结果，什么灵感、即兴、气质，我一概不懂。
cues.en: The writer George Moore recorded that Degas would say: "No art was ever less spontaneous than mine. What I do is the result of reflection and study of the great masters; of inspiration, spontaneity, temperament, I know nothing."

cues.zh: 看起来像随手抓到的一瞬间，在他自己看来，却是想出来、学出来的。
cues.en: A moment that looks caught by chance was, as he saw it, thought out and learned.

cues.zh: 他想的是什么？学的是什么？在乎的是什么？
cues.en: What was he thinking about? What was he learning? What did he care about?

cues.zh: 德加被称为「画舞女的画家」。我们看看他的作品，是真的吗？
cues.en: Degas has been called the painter of dancing girls. Let's look at his work. Is it true?

cues.zh: 德加对画商沃拉尔说过：人家都叫我「画舞女的画家」。他们从来没想到，我画舞者，最感兴趣的是画出动作，画好看的衣服。
cues.en: Degas once told the art dealer Ambroise Vollard: "People call me the painter of dancing girls. It has never occurred to them that my chief interest in dancers lies in rendering movement and painting pretty clothes."

cues.zh: 1874 年的第一次展览，只有一位女画家：贝尔特·莫里索。
cues.en: At the first exhibition in 1874, there was just one woman painter: Berthe Morisot.

cues.zh: 她是马奈的好朋友，马奈画过她很多次。1874 年，她嫁给了马奈的弟弟。
cues.en: She was a good friend of Manet, who painted her many times. In 1874 she married his brother.

cues.zh: 莫里索最常画的，是她身边的生活：家人、孩子、花园和海边。
cues.en: Morisot most often painted the life around her: family, children, gardens and the seaside.

cues.zh: 这幅《摇篮》1874 年就在第一次展览上展出。画的是谁呢？
cues.en: The Cradle was in that first exhibition of 1874. Who is in it?

cues.zh: 画的是她的姐姐埃德玛，守着睡着的小女儿。
cues.en: Her sister Edma, watching over her sleeping baby daughter.

cues.zh: 她怎么画的那层纱？
cues.en: And how did she paint the gauze?

cues.zh: 没有一根一根画出纱的纹路，只用了几笔透明的白。
cues.en: Not thread by thread. Just a few strokes of see-through white.

cues.zh: 在她不少画里，笔触很快，有的地方甚至露出底下的画布，看起来像没画完。
cues.en: In many of her paintings the brushwork is quick. In places you can even see bare canvas. It looks unfinished.

cues.zh: 为什么呢？
cues.en: Why?

cues.zh: 她曾在自己的笔记本里写道：「我的心愿，只是想留住一点正在过去的东西。」
cues.en: In her notebook she wrote that her ambition was simply "to capture something of what passes."

cues.zh: 1876 年，评论家沃尔夫在报上骂这群人是「五六个疯子，其中有一个女人」。
cues.en: In 1876, the critic Albert Wolff sneered in a newspaper that the group was "five or six lunatics, one of them a woman."

cues.zh: 如果是你，被人这样骂，还会接着画、接着参展吗？
cues.en: If people called you that, would you keep painting, and keep showing your work?

cues.zh: 莫里索没有停下。八次展览，她参加了七次，只有 1879 年那次没去，因为女儿刚出生。
cues.en: Morisot kept going. She was in seven of the eight exhibitions, missing only 1879, when her daughter had just been born.

cues.zh: 雷诺阿的这幅《煎饼磨坊的舞会》，画的是星期天下午，巴黎人在露天的花园里跳舞。
cues.en: Renoir's Dance at the Moulin de la Galette shows Parisians dancing in an open-air garden on a Sunday afternoon.

cues.zh: 你看人们的衣服和脸上，有什么？
cues.en: Look at the people's clothes and faces. What do you see?

cues.zh: 一块一块的亮斑。当年有评论家觉得，人的形状都被这些光斑化掉了。
cues.en: Patches of bright light. Some critics back then felt these spots made people's shapes melt away.

cues.zh: 这些亮斑是从哪里来的呢？
cues.en: Where do these bright patches come from?

cues.zh: 是从头顶树叶间漏下来的阳光。
cues.en: Sunlight, slipping through the leaves overhead.

cues.zh: 去掉了每个人清晰的轮廓，他留下的是什么呢？
cues.en: Without a sharp outline around anyone, what did he keep?

cues.zh: 他身边的朋友记得他说过：一幅画应该是可爱的、快乐的、漂亮的，对，漂亮的！生活里烦人的事已经够多了，我们不必再去制造。
cues.en: Friends remembered him saying: "A picture should be something likeable, joyful and pretty. Yes, pretty! There are enough unpleasant things in life without us making more."

cues.zh: 雷诺阿的热情，是生活里的快乐。
cues.en: Renoir's passion was the joy of everyday life.

cues.zh: 到这里，你可能觉得印象派就是去掉形状、留下光。可有一个人，偏偏反着来。他就是塞尚。
cues.en: By now you might think Impressionism means leaving out shapes and keeping light. But one painter did the opposite: Cézanne.

cues.zh: 1874 年第一次展览，塞尚也在。可他想要的不一样。他晚年对年轻画家德尼说：我想把印象派变成像博物馆里的艺术那样，坚实、持久的东西。
cues.en: Cézanne was in the first exhibition of 1874 too. But he wanted something different. Late in life he told the young painter Maurice Denis: "I wanted to make of Impressionism something solid and durable, like the art of the museums."

cues.zh: 他画家乡的圣维克多山，画了几十遍。早年的这一幅，树、田、桥都认得出来。
cues.en: He painted Mont Sainte-Victoire, the mountain near his home, dozens of times. In this early one, you can still make out the trees, the fields, the bridge.

cues.zh: 晚年的这一幅，你还认得出来吗？
cues.en: And this late one. Can you still make it out?

cues.zh: 山和田野变成一块一块的色面，像搭积木一样。
cues.en: The mountain and fields have become blocks of color, like building blocks.

cues.zh: 塞尚说过：我要用一个苹果，让巴黎吃惊！再看这篮苹果，画得怎么样？
cues.en: Cézanne once said: "With an apple, I want to astonish Paris!" Now look at this basket of apples. What do you notice?

cues.zh: 桌子的边，左右两边对不上；酒瓶也有点歪。
cues.en: The edges of the table don't line up, left and right. The bottle leans a little.

cues.zh: 这是画错了吗？还是他根本不在乎过去的规矩？
cues.en: Did he get it wrong? Or did he simply not care about the old rules?

cues.zh: 他在 1904 年的信中写道：在一个橘子、一个苹果、一个球、一个人头上，都有一个最高的点；不管光、影、颜色的效果多么可怕，这个点总是离我们的眼睛最近。
cues.en: In a letter in 1904 he wrote: "In an orange, an apple, a ball, a head, there is a culminating point, and this point is always, in spite of the tremendous effects of light, shade and color, the closest to our eye."

cues.zh: 他还写过：要用圆柱体、球体、圆锥体来处理自然。
cues.en: He also wrote: treat nature by the cylinder, the sphere, the cone.

cues.zh: 同样是看风景，莫奈要找的，是那一瞬间的光；塞尚要找的，是永恒的结构。为什么两个人在乎的东西这么不一样？
cues.en: Looking at the same kind of landscape, Monet was after the light of one instant, and Cézanne after a lasting structure. Why did they care about such different things?

cues.zh: 在这些印象派画家眼中，什么是多余的？什么是特别的？他们觉得什么重要呢？什么不重要呢？
cues.en: In the eyes of these Impressionist painters, what was unnecessary? What was special? What did they think mattered, and what didn't?

cues.zh: 马奈说，要画自己的时代、自己看到的东西；莫奈说，他要找的是瞬间和光；德加说，他靠的是思考和研究；
cues.en: Manet said: be of your own time, and paint what you see. Monet: instantaneity, and light. Degas: reflection and study.

cues.zh: 莫里索说，要留住正在过去的东西；雷诺阿说，画要可爱、快乐；塞尚说，要坚实、持久。
cues.en: Morisot: capture something of what passes. Renoir: a picture should be likeable and joyful. Cézanne: something solid and durable.

cues.zh: 他们的画，传达了他们在乎的信息。
cues.en: Their paintings carry the information they cared about.

cues.zh: 信息论的创始人香农在 1948 年的论文里写过，英文大约有一半是冗余的，删掉一部分字母，别人还能补回来。
cues.en: Claude Shannon, the founder of information theory, wrote in 1948 that ordinary English is roughly half redundant: delete some of the letters, and someone else can still restore them.

cues.zh: 试试看，这句话少了几个字，你补得出来吗？
cues.en: Try it. This sentence is missing some letters. Can you fill them in?

cues.zh: 这，也是印象派的秘密：先知道自己爱什么，才知道什么可以去掉。
cues.en: That is the secret of Impressionism too: first know what you love, and then you'll know what you can leave out.

cues.zh: 去掉了一部分冗余的信息，别人还能看懂吗？
cues.en: Leave out some of the redundant information, and can others still understand?

cues.zh: 1865 年人人嘲笑的《奥林匹亚》，二十五年后的 1890 年，正是克劳德·莫奈挺身而出，发起了一场公众募捐运动。
cues.en: In 1890, twenty-five years after everyone laughed at Olympia, it was Claude Monet who stepped forward and started a public fund to buy it.

cues.zh: 从马奈的遗孀手中买下了这幅作品，并将其赠送给了国家，最终在 1907 年让这幅曾经备受唾弃的艺术品堂堂正正地进入了卢浮宫。
cues.en: They bought it from Manet's widow and gave it to the nation, and in 1907 the painting people had once scorned took its place in the Louvre.

cues.zh: 画上一笔都没变。变的，是看画的人吗？
cues.en: Not one brushstroke changed. Was it the viewers who changed?

cues.zh: 那么，如果让你只用几笔，画下今天最想记住的一刻，你会去掉什么？留下什么？为什么偏偏是它？
cues.en: So, if you could use just a few strokes to paint the moment you most want to remember today, what would you leave out? What would you keep? And why that?

cues.zh: 这也是我们在 Lucas Academy 一起学习、一起思考的问题。
cues.en: That's what we learn and think about together at Lucas Academy.
